headline: Desert Tortoises Find Refuge in Nevada's Massive Solar Farm
meta_description: Threatened desert tortoises are thriving at Nevada's 7,100-acre Gemini Solar Project, using solar panels for shade while USGS documents their presence.
summary_short: Threatened desert tortoises have found an unexpected home at Nevada's Gemini Solar Project, where they use the solar panels as shelter.
body:
Threatened desert tortoises are now living inside Nevada's 7,100-acre Gemini Solar Project, using the solar panels for shade. The U.S. Geological Survey has been photographing the tortoises in their new habitat, documenting how they've adapted to the industrial landscape.

The project's developers took proactive steps to support the vulnerable species. Sections of the fence surrounding the solar installation were raised eight inches—a deliberate modification that allows the tortoises safe passage while protecting the installation.

The discovery reveals an unexpected benefit of large-scale renewable energy development: when designed thoughtfully, solar farms can coexist with wildlife. Rather than displacing the threatened species, the Gemini Solar Project has become a refuge where these desert dwellers can thrive beneath the very technology that harnesses the desert sun.
quick_facts: Nevada's Gemini Solar Project spans 7,100 acres
USGS photographing tortoises using solar panels for shade
Fence sections raised eight inches for tortoise passage
